messages:
maria (Sales): Quick heads-up — large enterprise on our POC wants to purchase via AWS Marketplace but procurement insists on PO routing to their corporate entity. They also want commit discounts and a consolidated invoice. We're mid-POC; what are the blockers?

alex (SE): Quick Q — are they trying to use a Standard Marketplace SKU or a Private Offer? Commit pricing + vendor invoices usually require a Private Offer.

maria (Sales): They said they prefer standard marketplace so procurement can use their internal marketplace flow, but they also asked for commit discounts (volume commit for 12mo). Sounds contradictory.

jon (Finance): FYI: Standard marketplace purchases are invoiced by AWS (they handle tax and remittance). If the customer needs vendor-issued invoices + commit discounts, we need a Private Offer or an off-market contract. For PO routing to their entity and consolidated billing we also need invoice mapping (SKU -> our internal rate card). Action items: we need customer billing entity name, tax ID/EIN, PO terms (Net30/Net45), and preferred cadence (monthly/annual).

alex (SE): For the POC itself: marketplace metering will show raw usage per SKU which makes seat-based or usage-based commits messy. Recommend we present two scenarios in the commercial: (1) Marketplace pricing (no vendor invoice, AWS handles tax) and (2) Private Offer with commit, vendor invoice and flexible tax handling. Include an expected cost projection for both.

rita (RevOps): Deal desk checklist: submit PRD in the deals portal with proposed commit amount, discount %, start/end dates, and PO sample. Attach procurement emails. This needs RevOps + Finance sign-off for any non-standard discounts, then Legal for addendum. Note: AWS Private Offer provisioning + procurement approvals can take 7–14 business days.

olivia (Legal): We need the customer's PO and the signed MSA (or redlines). If they want vendor invoices we must execute a Private Offer + MSA addendum. Also confirm any data residency / export-control clauses for the account. No immediate legal blockers but timeline depends on how quickly procurement returns the exemption cert and MSA signatures.

maria (Sales): They also asked about tax handling — they claim tax-exempt status. Jon, can we honor tax-exempt on a Private Offer?

jon (Finance): Yes, on Private Offers we can set tax handling per-customer, but we must collect an exemption certificate before issuing the first vendor invoice. On Standard Marketplace, AWS collects tax and we have no control.

alex (SE): Operational note for the POC — recommend we put the customer on a sandbox/limited plan to avoid surprise charges. Example snippet for the SE onboarding doc: 
```
# billing guardrail example
billing_cap: 5000  # USD monthly cap for POC
alert: finance@company.com
```

rita (RevOps): :thumbsup: I'm going to open the deals portal entry now and tag this as "Marketplace -> Private Offer migration." Maria — drop procurement contact + a redacted PO here so I can attach it.

maria (Sales): @rita added procurement contact in DM and posting a redacted PO here: ```PO-3219 | Acme Corp | Net30 | Billing entity: Acme Holdings | EIN: XX-XXXXXXX```

jon (Finance): Thanks — I'll prefill the invoice mapping template and set up a 15-min sync with their procurement team to confirm tax exemption and invoicing routing. If we get the PO + exemption cert this week we can target a Private Offer draft next week.

olivia (Legal): I'll standby for the MSA + addendum once you share the PO and contract redlines.

maria (Sales): Great — let's aim for the Private Offer draft next week. I'll keep you posted after the procurement call.
